issues.display_title: Issue #819: fix(wizard): an empty imported floor dead-ends Step 3 — the plan gate reads geometry, not provenance (#784)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-819.mp4

Source bug: #784 (reporter's video + mappedin-multi-building.zip)

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What actually happens

Step 3 ("Floor order & heights") disables Continue with "Every floor needs a name and a plan — uploaded or imported — to continue." after a multi-building Mappedin export is imported. The wizard dead-ends: Step 3 offers no per-floor delete, so the only way out is Back → Step 2 → remove floors one by one.

The extra floor in the issue title is not the trigger. Import-only exits through Continue to Editor (StepUploadFloor.tsx:158-215), which skips Steps 3 and 4 entirely. The only route to Step 3 with an import is Add More Floors — which is exactly what a user does when they want to add one more plan. Measured on the reporter's own file: the gate is already false before anything is uploaded, and the uploaded floor is the one config that passes it (it has a serverPath).

Zero-upload control, ~20 s in the UI: import → Add More Floors → upload nothing → Step 2 Continue enabled, Step 3 Continue still disabled.

Root cause

allFloorConfigsReady (src/lib/projects/wizardProject.ts:108-119), read at StepListFloor.tsx:38 and driving disabled={!floorsReady} at :188:

config.name.trim() && (config.serverPath.trim() || (config.id ? floorHasGeometry(canvasData, config.id) : false))

Imported floors always carry serverPath: "" (runImport.ts:52), so they hang entirely on floorHasGeometry, which is walls-or-areas only (wizardProject.ts:85-92).

The reporter's export contains four floors with no geometry at all — geometry/<id>.geojson is {"type":"FeatureCollection","features":[]}, 42 bytes. Both parking stacks ship geometry for the ground floor only; the upper decks are listed in floor-stacks.json and floors.geojson but are empty. The converter still emits a level for each, indistinguishable from createBlankLevel, so both branches of the gate are false.

Ran the production pipeline over the issue's own ZIP (parse → convert → extractFloors → groupBuildings → mergeImportIntoProject → gate):

staged configs: 15 | levels: 15 | buildings: 5
configs failing the gate: 4 of 15
  f_554be9cb38c56712 "Level 2" serverPath="" walls=0 areas=0   Multifamily Parking
  f_3223273b9641cd64 "Level 3" serverPath="" walls=0 areas=0   Multifamily Parking
  f_54172ce3fdbfc1fb "Level 4" serverPath="" walls=0 areas=0   Multifamily Parking
  f_3411bab0f9de9d43 "Level 2" serverPath="" walls=0 areas=0   Office Parking
GATE after import only:      false
GATE after adding one image: false

floorHasGeometry is a proxy for "this floor came from an import" — its own comment says so (#665: imported floors carry serverPath: "", so demanding an image stranded every importing project). A floor that came from an import but happens to be empty is exactly the case the proxy reads wrong.

Scope

  • Make the proxy exact. The gate accepts a floor whose level belongs to a building with imported: true — the flag is already on canvasData.buildings (mergeIntoProject.ts:103), so no new field and no change to the rule for uploads. An empty imported floor is a legitimate floor of the source and reaches the editor as a blank level the user can draw on.
  • Stop Step 2 and Step 3 disagreeing on "has content". objectCountOf (attachObjectCounts.ts:13-25) counts eight channels — walls, areas, points, shapes, safetyAnnotations, panoramas, doors, windows — while floorHasGeometry counts two. Step 2 can advertise a floor as "556 objects" while Step 3 calls it planless. Bites hardest on kind-less exports (#728), where geometry lands in shapes. Widen floorHasGeometry to the same channels.
  • Name the blocking floors. One flat boolean over 15 floors across 5 buildings, and the user has to guess which one. The message should say which floors — and which building they are in.

Acceptance

  • Importing mappedin-multi-building.zip and taking Add More Floors reaches Step 3 with Continue enabled, with no floor deleted
  • The four empty parking floors survive into the editor as blank, drawable levels — they are not dropped
  • A genuinely planless uploaded floor still blocks Continue (the rule for uploads is unchanged)
  • A floor Step 2 counts as having objects is never called planless by Step 3
  • When Continue is blocked, the message names the offending floors and their buildings
  • Regression test over the real export asserting allFloorConfigsReady(staged.floorConfigs, staged.canvasData) === true — a working probe is parked at .playwright-mcp/issue-784/probe.test.ts
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Found alongside — NOT in this scope

floors.geojson in the same export has 16 features; floor-stacks.json lists 15. f_2b5e14e618dfef00 ("Overview", 16 KB of real geometry — 11 Polygon, 6 Point) belongs to no stack, and parse.ts:116 builds floorIds as buildings.flatMap(b => b.floorIds) — so it never becomes a floor, a level, or a row. groupBuildings.ts:48-51's trailing group for leftovers never fires, because the leftover was discarded a stage earlier. That is silent data loss on import and wants its own issue.

Workaround until this ships

Back to Step 2 and delete the four empty parking floors (handleRemoveImportedFloor, StepUploadFloor.tsx:264-274), then continue.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/784-multi-building-add-floor, commit 0b1672f. Not pushed yet.

Scope changed during the work — two corrections to the plan above

1. Widening floorHasGeometry to eight channels turned out to be the wrong fix, and unnecessary. It has exactly two callers, and both want provenance, not geometry. Replacing the proxy at both settles the Step 2/Step 3 disagreement by construction: an imported floor now passes regardless of which channel its content landed in, so a kind-less export (#728) whose geometry sits in shapes can no longer be called planless. floorHasGeometry survives only as the fallback inside floorHasOwnPlan, and is no longer exported — leaving the wrong answer public beside the right one is how this reappeared after #665.

2. The same root cause broke Step 4 as well, which the task did not know. StepGenerate.tsx:313 fed importedFloorCount from the same proxy, and checklist.ts:56 computes floorCount === uploadedImageCount + importedFloorCount. On the reporter's file that came out 15 ≠ 0 + 11, so the pre-flight card claimed floors were missing on a complete project — #665's own symptom, reached through the same wrong question. Fixed with the gate.

While fixing it, a pre-existing drift surfaced: uploadedImageCount counted uploadedFiles while floorCount counted floorConfigs, and Step 3's delete (removeFloorConfig) drops a config and leaves the file list untouched. Both halves now read off floorConfigs, so the sum reconciles by construction.

What landed

File Change
lib/projects/wizardProject.ts floorIsImported (level → building → imported), floorHasOwnPlan = imported ‖ geometry, blockingFloors (one source of truth with allFloorConfigsReady), buildingNameOfFloor, shared GateCanvas type; floorHasGeometry un-exported
components/setup/StepListFloor.tsx gate + hint read the blockers; hint tied to the button with aria-describedby
lib/wizard/blockingFloorMessage.ts (new) the hint itself — grouped by building, long stacks capped, the two failures kept in separate clauses
components/setup/StepGenerate.tsx + step-generate/checklist.ts checklist counts provenance, and both halves off floorConfigs

Verification

pnpm test 189 files / 1690 tests · pnpm lint 0 errors · tsc --noEmit clean.

Run against the reporter's own export through the production pipeline (parse → convert → extractFloors → groupBuildings → mergeImportIntoProject → gate):

staged configs: 15 | levels: 15 | buildings: 5
configs failing the OLD geometry-only rule: 4 of 15
GATE after import only:      false -> true
GATE after adding one image: false -> true

The four empty parking decks survive into the editor as blank, drawable levels rather than being dropped.

Regression tests — 12 new assertions across two files: provenance read off the building not the geometry; an unstamped level must not inherit an imported building's provenance; an empty imported deck passes while a planless upload still blocks; geometry kept as the fallback for an import with no flag; blockingFloors is exactly the negation of the button's own predicate; and eight cases pinning the hint's copy — including that a floor which HAS an image is never told to upload one.

There is no end-to-end fixture: samples/ is gitignored (.gitignore:47), so the reporter's 3.9 MB export cannot be committed. The probe that runs it is parked at .playwright-mcp/issue-784/probe.test.ts; drop it into src/lib/mappedin-import/__tests__/ to re-run it locally.

Reviewed

Three independent adversarial reviewers over the diff (correctness, regression, copy), 21 findings, each put to a separate verifier instructed to refute. One survived — two new files still untracked at commit time, handled with git add -A. Fixed during the pass, from the rest: the hint reported the two failures as a conjunction (telling a floor with an image to upload one); join(", and ") repeated the conjunction per group; buildingNameOfFloor invented a second membership rule and could name a different building than the list beneath it; the button's title still carried the old flat copy; "upload an image" named a control that does not exist on Step 3; and the checklist count drift above.

Known limit, documented in the code

floorIsImported reads building MEMBERSHIP, not a per-floor origin stamp. A blank floor created while an imported building is selected would answer true. That is the same trade fillMissingLevels already makes when it mints Main Building so uploads cannot land in an imported building; closing it properly needs a persisted per-floor flag, worth doing the day a floor can be created into an imported building from the wizard — which today it cannot.

Still open — needs its own issue

The silently dropped "Overview" floor (f_2b5e14e618dfef00, 16 KB of real geometry, in no floor stack) is untouched, as scoped.

issues.display_title: Issue #829: fix(storage): a full localStorage kills project creation — one unguarded pointer write, three leaking blobs (#828)
issues.main_description_html:
Source bug: #828 (reporter's screenshot)

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What actually happens

Step 1 of the scan wizard shows a red box reading, verbatim:

Failed to execute 'setItem' on 'Storage': Setting the value of 'gf_project_id' exceeded the quota.

The wizard stays on Step 1. gf_project_id is a 36-byte UUID pointer — it is the victim of a full origin, not its cause.

The project row is already created when this fires. createProject (wizardProject.ts:34) resolves before the write at :41, so every retry commits another orphan draft server-side while the screen says creation failed.

"Cannot create a project" is narrower than the title, and wider than the wizard. Three separate corrections:

  • NewProjectFlow.tsx:145-160 ("Start from an empty canvas") works fine on a full origin — it never writes the pointer.
  • StepUploadFloor.tsx:193 hits the same unguarded write, but its catch at :210 renders "We couldn't create the project for this import. Check your connection and try again." — a network-flavoured message for a storage fault, row already orphaned.
  • useWizardPersistence.ts:64 calls the same setter inside the editor's restore useEffect, above let cancelled = false. On a full origin every /editor/<projectId> mount throws before any hydration — the editor is dead, not just the wizard. preview/[projectId]/page.tsx:34 is the same line.

Root cause — the throw site

src/store/mapStore/projectSlice.ts:55:

setProjectId: (id) => {
  if (typeof window !== "undefined") localStorage.setItem("gf_project_id", id);  // no try/catch
  set({ projectId: id });
},

This is the only unguarded setItem on the reported flow. Every writer that can actually fill the quota already swallows QuotaExceededError — useWizardPersistence.ts:133, history.ts:28, EditorTopbar.tsx:146 — which is exactly why the message names this 36-byte key and not the megabyte blob beside it. Chrome names the key being written, never the key that filled the origin.

The write also lands before set({ projectId: id }), so on throw the Zustand store never learns the id either. setCurrentSetupStep(1) at wizardProject.ts:42 never runs. Nothing recovers the id on reload: the pointer was not written, and the autosave blob carries state.projectId, which is still null. completeWizard.ts:47-49 already documents this dead end — "it only retries on the 0→1 transition, so it never recovers within a session."

Four more unguarded byte-scale writes throw the same way once the origin is full: completeWizard.ts:58, ProjectViews.tsx:51, EmptyCanvasPointer.tsx:79/90, FloorplanEditor.tsx:669.

Root cause — why the origin is full

Ran the production import pipeline over the sample exports in samples/ and measured exactly what reaches localStorage. Quota is ~5 MB per origin.

key contents measured
fp_history:<level_id> 40 undo + 40 redo full model snapshots, per level 3.2 MB (largest level, 628-hi-rise) · 11.9 MB (largest level, mappedin-multi-building)
gothru_wizard:<projectId> full canvasData + generatedTwin, per project 85 KB → 1.7 MB (36 levels)
gf_canvas_fallback full canvasData ~1.7 MB

A single large level exceeds the whole quota on its own through fp_history. Three leaks keep it there:

1. fp_history:* is swept only on a clean React unmount. clearEditorStorage (ClearEditorHistoryOnLeave.tsx:38-49) runs from an unmount cleanup. Tab close, refresh, or crash never runs it, so the stacks survive into the next session. PERSIST_MAX = 40 (history.ts:18) caps count, which means nothing when one snapshot is 305 KB.

2. gothru_wizard:<projectId> has no working eviction path at all. The only keyed removal (useWizardPersistence.ts:76) is unreachable for any project that has ever been saved: the editor path returns at :105 as soon as getFloorplanAction yields a server blob, so restoreFromLocal never runs. completeWizard.ts:61 removes the unkeyed gothru_wizard only, and says so in its own comment. gs_session (proxy.ts:62-72) lives 30 days and is minted only when absent. Growth is O(projects ever opened in the editor).

3. gf_canvas_fallback is write-only. EditorTopbar.tsx:145 writes ~1.7 MB on any save failure. Repo-wide grep returns the const at :44 and that one write — no getItem, no removeItem anywhere. Up to a third of the quota parked permanently for a consumer that does not exist.

Which writer lands the fatal byte

Verified in real headless Chrome: an origin saturated by a coarse writer still accepts a 36-byte setItem — the free space left over equals that writer's own increment. The write only fails once something has grown a value in small steps.

The fine-grained grower here is useWizardPersistence.ts:129, which re-serialises the whole blob on every store change. As the user types the project name on /start, it creeps forward a few bytes per keystroke until free space is under 36 bytes. Its silent catch {} at :133 is therefore part of the cause, not a mitigation — it sands away the last of the headroom without a sound.

Consequence for the fix: purging gothru_wizard:* alone will not recover a wedged origin. The whole family has to be swept.

Caveat kept honest: Blink emits this same string for non-quota storage failures (unreachable Local Storage backend, disk full), so the message pins the throw site, not the fill level.

Scope

  1. No byte-scale write may take a flow down. One shared guarded helper for the five unguarded writers (projectSlice.ts:55, completeWizard.ts:58, ProjectViews.tsx:51, EmptyCanvasPointer.tsx:79/90, FloorplanEditor.tsx:669). Guard the shared key, not each call site — completeWizard.ts:58 throws out of a live useMapStore.subscribe listener (useWizardPersistence.ts:344) when the AI scan finishes, and before StepGenerate.tsx:109's router.push, which is a worse failure than the reported one. In projectSlice, set() moves ahead of the storage write so the store is correct even when persistence is not.
  2. Delete the gf_canvas_fallback write. Nothing reads it. Deletion, not a guard.
  3. One editor draft blob, not one per project. Drop gothru_wizard:<other> when writing gothru_wizard:<current>.
  4. Bound fp_history by bytes, not by count, and sweep stale keys on editor entry as well as exit, so a tab close does not carry a full origin into the next session.

Acceptance

  • With the origin filled to quota, Step 1 Confirm Location advances to Step 2 and creates exactly one project
  • With the origin filled to quota, /editor/<projectId> mounts and hydrates
  • No repeated Confirm click creates a second project row for the same wizard run
  • gf_canvas_fallback no longer written; no reader existed
  • Opening project B leaves at most one gothru_wizard:<id> behind
  • Editing a level whose snapshot is ~300 KB does not saturate the origin
  • Unit tests: a throwing Storage stub does not break setProjectId, completeWizard, or the dashboard open handler; the eviction sweep keeps the current project's blob and drops the rest
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Measurement probes

Parked at .playwright-mcp/issue-828/ — probe.test.ts (wizard blob size), probe-history.test.ts (fp_history entry size), sizes.txt (the numbers above). Drop either into src/lib/mappedin-import/__tests__/ to re-run.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/829-localstorage-quota — commits 32403f9 and 4419447. PR #830 → development.

Before / after against a real wedged origin

Same wedge both sides: 25 decoy level mirrors, origin at 5,120 KB. The overlay is injected by the capture script, never by app code — without it the pair proves nothing, because a full origin looks identical to an empty one on screen.

development this branch
error the reported string, verbatim none
wizard stuck on Select Location reaches Upload Floor Plans
gf_project_id null written
fp_history keys 25 0
origin used 5,120 KB 120 KB

Screenshots and the capture script are at .playwright-mcp/demo/829/ — before-2-after-confirm.png, after-2-after-confirm.png, shots.mjs. (.playwright-mcp/ is gitignored, so they are not in the diff.)

No video: this bug has no visible "before" of its own, so a clip would have shown a working form and proved nothing. The storage readout is what carries the evidence, and a still frame holds it fine.

What landed

File Change
lib/persistence/safeStorage.ts (new) safeSetItem — guarded write; on a full origin drops the undo mirrors and retries once. clearEditorStorage moved here from the React component, so what counts as disposable lives beside the code that disposes of it
store/mapStore/projectSlice.ts set() before the storage write, and through the guard
wizard/completeWizard.ts, dashboard/ProjectViews.tsx, editor/EmptyCanvasPointer.tsx ×2, editor/FloorplanEditor.tsx the four remaining unguarded byte-scale writers route through the same helper
floorplanEditor/editor/history.ts mirror capped by bytes as well as steps; new persistable
persistence/wizardSession.ts dropOtherEditorBlobs — one editor draft, not one per project
editor/EditorTopbar.tsx the gf_canvas_fallback write deleted; nothing read it

Scope changed during the work — three corrections to the plan above

1. The plan's ranking of the bulk consumers was wrong in a way that matters. The task blamed gothru_wizard:<projectId> first. Measuring the real pipeline output put fp_history:<level_id> far ahead — 3.2 MB for the densest 628-hi-rise level and 11.9 MB for the densest mappedin-multi-building level, i.e. one level over the whole quota by itself. PERSIST_MAX = 40 caps count, which says nothing when one snapshot is 305 KB. That is why the fix caps by bytes and why the reclaim path targets fp_history rather than the wizard blob.

2. A fixed redo budget silently killed redo on exactly the levels the cap is for. Undo took three quarters of the budget and redo a fixed quarter. One dense-level snapshot is larger than that quarter, and persistable keeps nothing rather than something that does not fit — so every save wrote redo: [], and switching level and back left Ctrl+Shift+Z dead with the user's undone edits unrecoverable. Redo now takes whatever undo leaves, with the total cap unchanged.

3. The sweep leaked, and only the browser showed it. Sweeping 25 mirrors left 3 behind — 600 KB of exactly the space the sweep exists to free — so a reclaim reported success while the origin stayed near quota. Chrome does not enumerate localStorage in insertion order (a wedged origin starts at demo-level-19), and removeItem invalidates the cached key list, so removing inside the index walk re-orders what is left and skips entries. The inherited downward-walk shape hid this while the key set was small: a 26-key stub sweeps clean. Both sweeps now collect the doomed keys first and remove them after.

One more correction, to a comment rather than to behaviour: the byte budget was first written against "the stored JSON runs roughly double the raw snapshots". Measured on real snapshots it is 1.12–1.14×, so the budget went from 512 KB to 1 MB.

Trade-off worth knowing

Cross-reload undo gets shorter on mid-sized levels: 40 steps → ~26 at a 29 KB snapshot, 9 at 82 KB. On the densest sampled level (305 KB) it is 2 — but it was 0 before, because the 12 MB write was always refused.

Verification

pnpm test 191 files / 1708 tests · pnpm lint clean · tsc --noEmit clean.

Tests: a Storage stub with a real byte ceiling drives the reclaim-and-retry, the give-up path, and the write-your-own-history-key case; setProjectId keeps the id when storage throws; the byte cap is pinned in both directions; a Storage whose view reverses on every removal pins the sweep.

Both new behaviours are mutation-checked — restoring the fixed redo quarter fails the redo test, restoring the inline removal fails the sweep test — so neither test passes by accident.

Reviewed

Three independent adversarial reviewers over the diff (correctness, regression, coverage), 12 findings, each handed to a separate verifier instructed to refute it. Eleven fell. The survivor was correction 2 above. Correction 3 was found afterwards, by running the fix against a real browser rather than a stub — worth noting that no amount of review over the diff would have surfaced it.

Acceptance

  • With the origin filled to quota, Step 1 Confirm Location advances to Step 2 and creates exactly one project
  • With the origin filled to quota, /editor/<projectId> mounts and hydrates — the same unguarded write sat above the restore effect
  • No repeated Confirm click creates a second project row for the same wizard run
  • gf_canvas_fallback no longer written; no reader existed
  • Opening project B leaves at most one gothru_wizard:<id> behind
  • Editing a level whose snapshot is ~300 KB does not saturate the origin
  • Unit tests for the throwing-Storage paths and the eviction sweep
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Still open — not in this scope

gothru_wizard:stale-project is visible in the "after" screenshot at 119 KB: dropOtherEditorBlobs runs on an editor open, and this flow never reaches one. Correct as designed — the sweep is bounded to where "which project is current" has an answer — but it does mean a stale editor blob outlives a wizard-only session.

issues.display_title: Issue #822: feat(preview): a leading logo slot on every search result row (#779)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-822-search-logo-slot.mp4

Source PRD: #779 · Design: #782 · Design branch: design/multi-place-direction

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

A leading slot on every search result row: the place's logo when it has one, a map pin when it does not. R1-R10, R16-R22.

No data-model work. Information.logo?: string already exists (src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:181) and the search rows already read target.info — today they render text only (src/components/editor/preview/SearchAreaPanel.tsx:160-201, a min-h-14 column of title + kind badge + floor badge + description).

Scope

Take the design branch's implementation, do not rewrite it

design/multi-place-direction already carries this half in full and it is the ONLY half of #779 that lands cleanly: its SearchAreaPanel.tsx hunk was diffed against development on 27 Aug and the pre-image matches the current file byte for byte. Two files come across:

  • src/components/editor/preview/PlaceLogo.tsx (new, 74 lines)
  • src/components/editor/preview/SearchAreaPanel.tsx (row restructured into slot + text column, flex-col → items-center gap-3)

The slot

  • Fixed size-10, shrink-0, rounded, bordered, opaque frame — a logo brings its own background (white / transparent / none), so it needs a surface or a white mark vanishes into the row (R3).
  • object-contain, never cover: a very wide or very tall logo is fitted, never cropped, and never resizes the slot (R4, D2).
  • The map pin is painted as the FLOOR of the slot, always, with the logo laid over it once decoded — that is what makes "no logo", "still loading" and "broken logo" one picture instead of three (R7, R9, R10). No layout shift on swap.
  • loading="lazy" so a long result list does not fetch every logo at once (F5).
  • onError → fall back to the pin. A logo URL can 404 long after upload (R9).
  • Re-used row: the src is the identity of what is shown, so the load state resets when it changes as the visitor types.
  • An image can finish loading before React attaches onLoad (cached logo, data URI, hydrated row) — read complete/naturalWidth on the node or a good logo sits at opacity 0 forever.

Do not touch

Category browser rows get NO leading slot (R19, D6). Matching, ordering and the zero-result copy stay exactly as they are (R16-R20, F6).

Tests

Port src/components/editor/preview/__tests__/SearchAreaPanel.leading-slot.test.tsx from the design branch: logo present / absent / errors; category rows unaffected; result ordering unchanged.

Notes

Independent of the whole Direction half — ships on its own, and the PRD's suggested order puts it first.

Watch the overlap with #789 ([PRD] Update Search Area Layout / Viewer Search Discovery, design #790 still open): that PRD rebuilds the same panel around categories / nearby / recent / suggestions. This task only adds the leading slot to the existing result row, so it stays a small rebase for whoever picks #789 up — do not pre-empt it here.

pnpm test / pnpm lint

issues.display_title: Issue #823: feat(routing): trip model — ordered places, multi-leg planning, totals and arrival times (#779)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-823-trip-model.mp4

Source PRD: #779 · Design: #782 · Design branch: design/multi-place-direction

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

The data half of multi-place Direction: an ordered list of places instead of one destination, a route planned leg by leg, and totals + arrival times derived from it. R24-R25, R32-R36, R52-R59. Blocks #824, #825, #826, #827.

Direction state today is single-destination: DirectionPanel.tsx:17 declares toArea: DirectionAreaEndpoint | null and the state touches exactly three files — src/components/editor/preview/DirectionPanel.tsx, src/components/editor/preview/useDirectionMapLayers.ts, src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx. fromMode / fromArea / fromPin are untouched by this task.

Scope

State

toArea → an ordered places array. Single place must behave exactly as today (R34) — that is the regression bar for this whole task.

Multi-leg planning

planMultiLevelRoute({canvasData, location, from, to}) (src/lib/routing/multiLevelRoute.ts:181) takes ONE origin and ONE destination. Multi-place is N-1 calls over consecutive pairs, concatenating segments and transfers. The routing engine itself does not change (R35).

Port trip.ts onto development's primitives — NOT the design branch's

design/multi-place-direction has src/lib/routing/trip.ts (228 lines, MAX_TRIP_PLACES, TripLeg, TripSummary, Trip, planTripLegs, buildTrip, addPlaceRefusal, movePlace) and it is the right shape — but it was branched at 90f1997 (21 Aug), BEFORE the route redesign landed, and it sits on a private copy of the route primitives that development has since built differently:

design branch (routeSteps.ts, 248 lines) development, already merged
WALK_SPEED_MPS WALKING_PACE_MPS — src/lib/routing/routeDistance.ts:17
LIFT_TRANSFER_SECONDS, STAIRS_SECONDS_PER_FLOOR same names — routeDistance.ts:21,24
hasRealScale() isScaledProject() — routeDistance.ts:44
pathMeters() routeMetrics() — routeDistance.ts:73
buildRouteDetail() / RouteDetail buildRouteSteps() / RouteStep — src/lib/routing/routeSteps.ts:57

F10 is explicit: define the constants ONCE and share them with the route redesign work. So do not port the design branch's routeSteps.ts — retarget planTripLegs / buildTrip at buildRouteSteps + routeMetrics + isScaledProject. MAX_TRIP_PLACES, addPlaceRefusal and movePlace are pure and come across as-is.

Totals and arrival times

  • Gate every total on isScaledProject / FloorplanMeta.scaleMmPerUnit (src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:98). An unscaled project drops distance and time entirely — no placeholder, no warning to the visitor (R59, D10).
  • Physics stays the inherited constants: 1.2 m/s walking, 60s per lift, 30s per floor of stairs (R52-R55).
  • Arrival time is cumulative per place; the final place's arrival equals the trip total (R56-R58).

Tests

Port src/lib/routing/__tests__/trip.test.ts (173 lines) retargeted at the development primitives: multi-leg concatenation; totals; cumulative arrival times; unscaled project shows no distance/time/arrival; single-place regression — identical output to the pre-change path.

Notes

Partial / failed legs are #827, not this task. Build the per-leg status field here, leave the suppression rules to that one.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

issues.display_title: Issue #824: feat(preview): trip place list — add, remove, reorder and the 8-place cap (#779)
issues.main_description_html:

The place list a visitor actually edits: add, remove, reorder, renumber. R26-R31, R38-R44, R56. Depends on #823 (trip state + MAX_TRIP_PLACES / addPlaceRefusal / movePlace).

Scope

Port src/components/editor/preview/TripPlaceList.tsx (227 lines) from the design branch and wire it into DirectionPanel.tsx in place of the single destination input. It already carries the row shape the design settled on: number badge, place name, floor badge (levelName, only set on multi-floor projects), arrival time, remove control, reorder affordance.

  • Add — the existing DirectionAreaAutocomplete is the picker; the design branch also touches it (+27 lines, plus a 46-line test). Take that with it.
  • Cap at 8 places (R26). The refusal is a message on the control, shown until the next add succeeds — not a disabled control with no explanation (R30, D9).
  • Duplicate rejected with its own reason (R31).
  • Reorder — the design branch picked the interaction (D8); take what it does rather than re-deciding it, and check it on touch: dragging inside a scrolling panel on a phone is the risk the PRD called out (R28).
  • Renumber on every change — add, remove and reorder all re-run the numbering (R43, R44). The numbers here are the same numbers the map markers draw (#825), so numbering lives in one place.
  • Long place names and long floor names must not break the row (R41, R56, D7).

Tests

8-place cap; duplicate rejection; renumbering after add / remove / reorder; a row survives a long place name and a long floor name.

Notes

Marker ↔ row highlight is #825 — TripPlaceListProps already has the selected hook for it (TripPlaceList.tsx:27), so leave the prop in and wire the map side there.

issues.main_description_html:
Source PRD: #779 · Design: #782 · Design branch: design/multi-place-direction

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Numbered markers on the map, and selection that runs both ways between a marker and its row. R61-R69. Depends on #823; pairs with #824 (the list those numbers come from).

Scope

Markers

Port src/lib/preview/tripMarkers.ts (101 lines: tripMarkerIndex, placeAnchor, tripMarkers) from the design branch and extend src/components/editor/preview/useDirectionMapLayers.ts to draw them.

  • Numbered per place, current floor only (R61).
  • Renumber whenever the list changes — the numbers are #824's numbers, not a second source (R63).
  • Number stays legible across map zoom levels (R62, D14).
  • Two places close enough to overlap stay individually selectable and never merge into a cluster (R63, D14).
  • Origin marker is visually distinct and never numbered, including the dropped-pin variant (R64, R65, D15).

Selection binding

Selecting a marker highlights its row; selecting a row focuses the map on that marker (R67, R68). Strictly read-only — selection never edits the trip (R69).

TripPlaceList already exposes the row side of this (selected prop, TripPlaceList.tsx:27).

Tests

Port src/lib/preview/__tests__/tripMarkers.test.ts (68 lines): numbering follows list order; renumber on change; origin unnumbered; current-floor filtering.
